title: "Comparing REQ vintages and forecast errors"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Comparing REQ vintages and forecast errors}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}
  %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8}
---

Revision operations are intentionally separate:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
observations <- rbind(
  read_req("req-2025-12", view = "reported"),
  read_req("req-2026-06", view = "reported")
)

history <- req_history_revision(observations)
forecast <- req_forecast_revision(observations)
first_error <- req_forecast_error(observations, realisation = "first")
latest_error <- req_forecast_error(
  observations, realisation = "latest_revised"
)
```

The comparison engine uses an internal status-independent semantic join key,
because public `series_id` deliberately includes status. Results retain old and
new public series IDs, statuses, status sources, hashes, issue dates, target
period bounds, issue-to-target horizons, selection rules and source provenance.
Unit, currency, price basis, period basis and geography must match. Non-unique
joins fail rather than choosing by row order.

Forecast revision requires the earlier observation to be a forecast or
projection. It compares that row with the next later comparable vintage, whose
status may be forecast, projection, estimate or historical. Consequently the
required December 2025 forecast to June 2026 estimate transition is retained
instead of being filtered out.

First-realisation error uses the first later estimate or historical value.
`latest_revised_error` is separately labelled and may change as history is
revised.
